visualInspection.result: All seven canonical screenshots were viewed. Form controls, translated actions and two placement/instance identity labels are readable at 390px with no horizontal overflow. Long group details and complete source use ordinary vertical scrolling.
visualInspection.scope: Images show visible form or identity-impact sections; complete candidate source and all generated identities/provenance are asserted from actual DOM and HTTP payloads, not screenshots alone.

reviewedBoundaries.detail: New optional structure ABI and addFragmentActor/removeFragmentActor dispatch are separate from old SET/RESET, offset and local/batch patch operations. The old protected 23 files are byte-identical; old single/batch run in new evidence directories.

ADD requires exactly one explicit instanceId for each related placement in source order. Generated IDs are chosen once per UI transaction, unchanged by raw editing and checks. Original and final full recipe expansion guard all identities, group references, local+offset bounds, 128 declared/expanded budgets and final 128KiB bytes before returning one edit receipt.

New IDs reject collisions with existing generated actor/group UUIDs and placement UUIDs; pure proposal additionally rejects selected scene UUID. Rust recipe content has no scene metadata UUID. Referenced definition objectId is a separate domain and repeated OC/projection references remain permitted.

REMOVE deletes the shared declaration, every related actorIds entry and the matching local override whole record. Empty overrides wrappers, unrelated override records/fields, group declarations and group identities remain. A fragment's last actor cannot be deleted, including unused fragments.

Factory binds the complete current preview once and checks ordered actor/group source provenance, actor objectId, recipe path/revision and real sceneStructure groups. Parent candidate matcher reconstructs source order from actual afterContent, requiring exact actor/group cardinality, unique identities and complete declaration ownership, so a removed selected actor does not block legitimate REMOVE.

Source and nested proposal snapshots occur before the asynchronous digest; accessors, serializers, cycles, non-JSON prototypes/values and malformed arrays reject. Apply recomputes canonical edit, all targets, exact full afterContent and ordered changedPaths from current source. UI raw and detached proposal signatures cannot reuse approval after silent edits.

Entry/validation/apply retain parent session, recipe/path, source-token, canEdit and child owner guards after awaits. Apply updates only in-memory source through the ordinary guarded receipt; normal Save retains baseline conflict handling. Actual external writes preserved both disk and reviewed local draft; cancellation made no author changes.

Complete source dependency enumeration visits objectId and explicit imageResourceId of all fragments including unused, plus local override images, before expansion. Placed candidate media bytes are resolved and sanitized by ordinary host preview. Actual missing registered image bytes blocked Check and Apply; no malicious SVG code/network request ran.

Unused fragments support source-only ADD/REMOVE with targets[] and no fabricated identities. Their declarations and explicit registered dependencies are checked; no expanded effective actor exists, so inherited runtime projection semantics and actual image rendering are deferred until placement. This preserves the established preview contract and does not claim unused rendering acceptance.

The three dynamic group/image placeholder options now carry data-i18n. Real zh-CN/en/ja changes preserve approved selection, raw values and both new UUIDs. All three 390px forms and impact labels fit horizontally; sticky Check/Apply/Cancel actions remain visible.
